title: Kosmos AI Scientist reads ~1,500 papers per run and reports seven discoveries
summary: Edison Scientific's Kosmos runs for up to 12 hours, coordinating data-analysis and literature-search agents through a shared world model to generate hypotheses and write cited scientific reports.
agent_role: Agents analyzed datasets, searched literature and drafted reports autonomously over a run; human scientists supplied the data and objective and evaluated the statements afterward.
outcome: About 200 agent rollouts, ~42,000 lines of code and ~1,500 papers read per run; independent scientists judged 79.4% of report statements accurate; seven showcased discoveries
what_they_did: Edison Scientific's team built Kosmos, an AI scientist that takes an open-ended objective and a dataset and runs for up to 12 hours. A data-analysis agent and a literature-search agent share findings through a structured world model, running cycles of analysis, literature search and hypothesis generation. Kosmos then writes reports that cite every statement to code or primary literature. Scientists supplied data and goals and checked the results.
how_it_went: The paper reports about 200 agent rollouts, 42,000 lines of code and 1,500 papers read per run on average. Independent scientists found 79.4% of report statements accurate, and collaborators said a 20-cycle run equaled about 6 months of their own research time. It highlights seven discoveries, three reproducing unpublished findings and four new.
worth_knowing: About one in five report statements was not judged accurate, so the citations to code and papers matter: they let you trace and check each claim.
prompt: I have a dataset at [file or folder] and this research objective: [objective]. Work in cycles. In each cycle, run an analysis on the data, search the published literature for related findings, and update a running notes file that lists hypotheses, evidence for and against, and open questions. Save all analysis code. After [number] cycles, write a short report where every claim cites either the specific code output or a paper with a link. Flag which findings look new and which repeat known results. Show me your plan for the first cycle before starting.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
